description:
**Everything before this is tested against doubles.** This is the first tasklist where real bytes cross a real wire to a real server.

The stack is already decided and is adopted, not built: `draft-ietf-httpbis-resumable-upload` (tus 2.x lineage, interop version pinned) against **tusd v2** with the **S3 backend**. `docs/reference/wire-protocol.md` is the contract; this tasklist proves both dialects actually speak it.

**The interesting assertions are the failure paths, not the happy one.** An upload that completes on a good network proves very little — the whole product thesis is what happens when it does not.

userStories.title: Both platforms complete an upload against a real tusd instance
userStories.description: create / head / append / terminate, in both dialects, against tusd v2 + S3.
acceptanceCriteria: A reproducible tusd v2 + S3 test environment is documented and scripted.
Both the Swift and Kotlin wire layers complete a multi-megabyte upload against it.
The pinned interop version is asserted — a server advertising a different version is rejected rather than guessed at.
`terminate` is proven to actually remove the server-side upload.

userStories.title: Resume works across an interruption, from the server's offset
userStories.description: The claim that justifies the project. An upload killed at 40% must resume at 40%, not restart.
acceptanceCriteria: An upload interrupted mid-transfer resumes from the offset the server reports via HEAD, not from a locally cached guess.
Resume is proven across PROCESS DEATH, not merely a cancelled task — kill the process, relaunch, assert the transfer continues.
The bytes that arrive at S3 are byte-identical to the source — verified by checksum, on both platforms.
A server that reports an unexpected offset is handled as a typed error, not by silently restarting.
